info.title: Restaurant operations platform API
info.description: Orders at the table, tickets live in the kitchen, a bill at the end.

get.summary: The admin's whole floor, live and archived, with each table's occupancy.
get.description:
# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` for a waiter or a chef, and
`503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: The whole floor, live and archived. Admins only.

post.summary: Adds a section to the end of the section list.
post.description:
It appears on the admin's screen at once, and on waiters' floors once it
holds a live table.

# Errors

Returns `400` naming the field that was not accepted, including
`fields.name=already_taken`, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a
waiter or a chef.

201.description: The section, at the end of the list. Admins only.

put.summary: Puts the sections in a new order, the order waiters then see.
put.description:
No audit row: a reorder changes no version, so it makes no open form stale.

# Errors

Returns `409 floor_changed` if the list is not exactly the live sections,
`401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

200.description: The live sections in their new order. Admins only.

409.description: `floor_changed`: the list is not the live set any more.

put.summary: Renames a section, provided nobody changed it since the form loaded.
put.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 section_changed` if the stored version is newer, `404` if
there is no such live section, `400` naming the field that was not
accepted, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The section to rename.

200.description: The renamed section. Admins only.

409.description: `section_changed`: somebody changed it after the form loaded.

post.summary: Takes a section off the floor. It moves to the Archived section.
post.description:
Refused while it still holds a live table, including one being created in,
moved into, or restored into it at the same instant.

# Errors

Returns `409 section_not_empty` if it holds a live table, `404` if there is
no such live section, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter
or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The section to remove.

200.description: The archived section. Admins only.

409.description: `section_not_empty`: it still holds a live table.

post.summary:
Puts an archived section back at the end of the list, with the chosen
archived tables that were in it, in one transaction.
post.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 name_taken` if a live section now has its name, `409
labels_taken` with `labels` if a chosen table's label is taken (either
refusal restores nothing), `400` if an id is not an archived table of this
section, `404` if there is no such archived section, `401` if nobody is
signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The archived section to put back.

200.description: The section, live again, and its restored tables. Admins only.

400.description: An id is not an archived table of this section.

409.description: `name_taken`, or `labels_taken` with the clashing `labels`.

put.summary: Puts one group's tables in a new order, the order waiters then see.
put.description:
A table cannot be dragged into another group here: moving it is an edit.

# Errors

Returns `409 floor_changed` if the list is not exactly that group's live
tables, `404` if the section is not a live one, `401` if nobody is signed
in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

200.description: The group's live tables in their new order. Admins only.

409.description: `floor_changed`: the list is not the live set any more.

post.summary: Adds one table to the end of its group.
post.description:
It appears on the admin's screen at once, and on every waiter's floor within
about two seconds.

# Errors

Returns `400` naming each field that was not accepted, including
`fields.label=already_taken`, `409 section_archived` if the section has been
archived, `404` for a section this restaurant does not have, `401` if nobody
is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

201.description: The table, at the end of its group. Admins only.

409.description: `section_archived`: that section is no longer on the floor.

post.summary:
Adds a numbered range of tables to the end of their group, every one or
none.
post.description:
# Errors

Returns `400` naming each field that was not accepted, `409 labels_taken`
with `labels` listing every generated label a live table already has (and
nothing created), `409 section_archived` if the section has been archived,
`404` for a section this restaurant does not have, `401` if nobody is
signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

201.description: The created tables, in number order. Admins only.

409.description: `labels_taken` with the clashing `labels`, or `section_archived`.

put.summary:
Edits a table's label, seats, or section, provided nobody changed it since
the form loaded.
put.description:
Allowed while a party sits at it. A changed label reaches every waiter's
floor, the waiter's table screen, and the kitchen's tickets within about two
seconds.

# Errors

Returns `400` naming each field that was not accepted, `409
section_archived` if the target section has been archived, `409
table_changed` if the stored version is newer, `404` if there is no such
live table or section, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter
or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The table to edit.

200.description: The table after the edit. Admins only.

404.description: No such live table or section.

409.description: `section_archived` or `table_changed`.

post.summary: Takes a table off the floor. It moves to the Archived section.
post.description:
Refused while a party sits at it, including one being seated at the same
instant. Every visit, round, ticket, and bill that named it still resolves.

# Errors

Returns `409 table_in_use` if it has an open visit, `404` if there is no
such live table, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a
chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The table to remove.

200.description: The archived table. Admins only.

409.description: `table_in_use`: a party is at it. Close the table first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The archived table to put back.

404.description: No such archived table or section.

409.description: `category_archived`: that category is no longer on the menu.

put.summary: Edits a dish, moving it when its category changes.
put.description:
The target category is checked before the version, so an edit that is both

Returns `400` naming each field that was not accepted, `409

parameters.name: id

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Registers a restaurant and signs its owner in as the admin.
post.description:
One transaction. Any failure inside it, a duplicate address in particular,
leaves no restaurant, no staff row, and no session: the transaction is
simply dropped, and everything it wrote goes with it.

The five settings the restaurant starts with come from the country's row in
`locales/countries.json` and from nowhere else.

# Errors

Returns a `400` naming each field that was not accepted, including
`fields.email=already_taken` for an address that already has an account, and
a `503` if the database or the password hash is unavailable.

200.description: The restaurant and its admin now exist, and the response sets the session cookie.

400.description: A field was not accepted. `fields.email=already_taken` when that address already has an account.

post.summary: Signs somebody in.
post.description:
The address is looked up across every restaurant, because sign in has a
chicken and egg problem: there is no restaurant to scope to until the
account is found. That lookup is one of exactly two in the system that read
across restaurants, and it is `SECURITY DEFINER` in the database with a
fixed narrow shape.

# Errors

Returns `401` for a wrong password, an address nobody has, and a deactivated
account alike, and a `503` if the database or the password hash is
unavailable.

200.description: Signed in, and the response sets the session cookie.

401.description: Identical for a wrong password and for an address nobody has.

post.summary: Signs out exactly the session that made the request.
post.description:
Every other session belonging to the same person keeps working, which is
what makes signing out on the house phone at the end of a shift safe to do.

# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, and a `503` if the database is
unavailable.

204.description: Signed out, and the response clears the cookie.

put.summary: Switches a dish on or off.
put.description:
Admins and chefs, and it is the only menu change a chef can make. Every
waiter's ordering screen greys the dish within a second or two, through the
`dish` event this write sends. Never refused as stale; setting the value it
already has succeeds and changes nothing.

# Errors

Returns `404` if there is no such live dish, including one archived a moment
earlier, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dish to switch.

200.description: The dish after the switch. Admins and chefs.

get.summary: Opens the live stream for the caller's restaurant.
get.description:
The stream carries only this restaurant's events, because the server routes
on the restaurant id before it ever writes to a socket. Sending everything
and letting the browser filter would leak ticket volume, timing, and
identifiers between restaurants over the wire, even though the follow up
fetch would be refused.

The client must refetch its active queries every time this opens, including
every reconnect. Postgres queues nothing for a listener that is not
connected, so anything sent during a gap is gone, and without a refetch one
network blip becomes a ticket that never appears in the kitchen.

200.description: A server sent event stream. Each message is named `entity_changed` and its data is a StreamEvent.

401.description: Nobody is signed in, so there is no restaurant to stream.

get.summary: The floor, in the order it is walked.
get.description:
# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` if the caller is not a waiter,
and `503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: Every live table and its occupancy. Waiters only.

get.summary: Reports whether this instance can actually serve.
get.description:
Returns 200 only when the pool answers **and** the listen connection is
alive. An instance whose listener has died still answers HTTP perfectly but
delivers no tickets to any kitchen screen, so a check that only proved the
process was up would leave it in service forever.

200.description: Every dependency is up and this instance can serve.

503.description: A dependency is down. Take this instance out of service.

get.summary: The kitchen queue: cooking oldest first, then plated oldest first.
get.description:
Carries the restaurant's own two thresholds with it rather than leaving the
screen to decide when a ticket is late, and says how many tickets it left
behind rather than quietly cutting them off.

# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` if the caller is not a chef, and
`503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: Up to 120 queued or ready tickets, cooking first, with this restaurant's ageing thresholds. Chefs only.

get.summary: Who is signed in, and where they work.
get.description:
The same bundle sign in returns, so a browser that has reloaded gets back to
exactly the state it had without a second endpoint or a second shape.

One of exactly two handlers that name `PasswordMayBeOwed`, and it has to be:
the bundle is where the browser reads that a password is owed, so gating
this one would leave a browser unable to find out why everything else was
refused.

# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, and a `503` if the database is
unavailable.

200.description: The signed in identity. Any signed in role, and reachable while a password change is owed.

patch.summary: Changes the caller's own display name or personal language.
patch.description:
# Errors

Returns a `400` naming the field that was not accepted, `401` if nobody is
signed in, and a `503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: The updated identity. Any signed in role, own row only.

post.summary: Changes the caller's own password, and signs their other devices out.
post.description:
The session that made the request keeps working, so somebody changing their
password on the screen in front of them is not immediately signed out of it.
Every other session of theirs is revoked in the same transaction, which is
what makes "I think somebody has my password" a thing they can act on alone.

The other of exactly two handlers that name `PasswordMayBeOwed`, and the
only way out of owing one. Somebody an admin created gives the password they
were handed as their current one, and this is what spends it: the flag is
cleared by the write itself, in the repository, so no path can set a
password without settling what was owed on it.

# Errors

Returns a `400` with `fields.currentPassword=incorrect` for a wrong current
password, `401` if nobody is signed in, and a `503` if the database or the
password hash is unavailable.

204.description: Changed. Any signed in role, own row only, and reachable while a password change is owed.

400.description: The current password was wrong, or the new one broke a rule.

get.summary: The restaurant's live menu, in printed order.
get.description:
# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` if the caller is neither a
waiter nor a chef, and `503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: The live menu. Waiters and chefs.

403.description: Neither a waiter nor a chef.

post.summary: Marks one dish off the pass.
post.description:
Touches that dish and nothing else. The ticket's own status follows from all
of its dishes and is recomputed inside the same transaction, which is why
nothing here sets it.

# Errors

Returns `409 line_not_queued` if another chef marked it first, `404` if
there is no such dish, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if the caller
is not a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dish to mark off the pass.

200.description: The dish and its ticket's new status. Chefs only.

409.description: Somebody marked that dish first.

post.summary: Marks one dish as having reached the table.
post.description:
Touches that dish only. A starter goes out the moment it is ready while the
main course on the same ticket is still cooking.

# Errors

Returns `409 line_not_ready` if the dish is not waiting to be carried out,
`404` if there is no such dish, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if
the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dish that reached the table.

200.description: The dish and its ticket's new status. Waiters only.

409.description: `line_not_ready`: that dish is not waiting to be carried out.

post.summary: Puts one plated dish back on the stove.
post.description:
The undo for [`mark_line_ready`], and the only way back from `ready` that is
not a waiter serving the food. A ticket that had gone ready returns to cooking
with the dish, recomputed in the same transaction, so the waiter's screen
corrects itself through the event rather than being told separately.

# Errors

Returns `409 line_not_ready` if the dish is not waiting to be carried out,
which is what a waiter serving it a moment earlier produces, `404` if there is
no such dish, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if the caller is not a
chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dish to put back on the stove.

200.description: The dish and its ticket's new status. Chefs only.

409.description: `line_not_ready`: that dish is not waiting to be carried out.

post.summary:
Cancels one dish that is still cooking or waiting on the pass, with a
reason, and takes it off the bill.
post.description:
**A waiter or a chef, and the two may give different reasons.** A waiter
cancels for any of the four: the guest changed their mind, it was entered by
mistake, the kitchen has run out, or something else they write down. A chef
may give one reason only, `kitchen_unavailable`, because that is the one thing
a kitchen knows that nobody else does. Why a guest changed their mind is not a
judgement to make from behind the pass.

**A chef giving any other reason is a `400`, not a `403`.** Every `403` in this
API is the role refusal the `Actor` extractor makes before the handler body
runs, and a chef calling this endpoint is allowed to call it. What is refused
is the value of one field, and a refused field value is a named field error
everywhere else here.

# Errors

Returns `400` if the reason is `other` with no words
(`fields.reason = required`), the words are over 200 characters
(`fields.reason = too_long`), or a chef gave any reason but kitchen
unavailable (`fields.reasonCode = not_allowed_for_chef`),
`409 line_not_voidable` if the dish has been served or already cancelled,
`404` if there is no such dish, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if the
caller is an admin.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dish to cancel.

200.description: The cancelled dish, its ticket, and the bill's subtotal after. Waiters, and chefs for kitchen unavailable only.

400.description: A missing or over long reason, or a reason a chef may not give.

409.description: `line_not_voidable`: that dish has been served or already cancelled.

get.summary: Every open table and every ticket on it.
get.description:
# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` if the caller is not a waiter,
and `503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: Every open visit with its tickets and dishes. Waiters only.

patch.summary: Changes the restaurant's settings. Admins only.
patch.description:
The role requirement is in the signature: `Actor<Admin>` refuses a waiter and
a chef with `403` before this body runs, so there is no line here to forget.

**The edit names the version it was made against**, and a stale one is refused
rather than merged. That covers all seven settings, not only the two kitchen
thresholds this endpoint grew in spec 0012: name, address, timezone, and the
two language fields come under the same conditional update.

**The two thresholds are merged over the stored pair before either is
checked.** Each may be edited on its own while the rule that amber comes
before red spans both, so an edit raising only the warning can cross a stored
late value it never mentions. The merge is what catches that, and it is what
lets a refusal name a field rather than say "those two are wrong".

# Errors

Returns a `400` naming each field that was not accepted, `409
restaurant_changed` if the version is no longer current, `403` for a waiter
or a chef, `401` if nobody is signed in, and a `503` if the database is
unavailable.

200.description: The updated identity, carrying the new version. Admins only.

403.description: A waiter or a chef asked.

409.description: `restaurant_changed`: somebody saved these settings first.

post.summary: Marks every dish still cooking on one ticket off the pass, in one go.
post.description:
One transaction, so the ticket either fully flips or does not change at all. A
chef who plates a whole table at once taps once instead of four times, and a
request that fails half way leaves every dish exactly as it was.

# Errors

Returns `409 round_not_queued` if no dish on the ticket is still cooking,
which is also what a colleague marking one of them between the read and the
write produces, `404` if there is no such ticket, `401` if nobody is signed
in, and `403` if the caller is not a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ticket whose cooking dishes are all done.

200.description: The ticket after the write. Chefs only.

409.description: `round_not_queued`: nothing on that ticket is still cooking.

post.summary: Marks every dish on a ticket that is waiting to be carried out.
post.description:
Serves what is ready and leaves what is still cooking, so a waiter carrying
out the starters on a ticket whose main is still on the stove taps once.

# Errors

Returns `409 nothing_ready` if no dish on the ticket is waiting to be
carried out, `404` if there is no such ticket, `401` if nobody is signed in,
and `403` if the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ticket whose ready dishes reached the table.

200.description: The ticket after the write. Waiters only.

409.description: `nothing_ready`: no dish on that ticket is waiting to be carried out.

get.summary: Everybody who works here. Admins only.
get.description:
# Errors

Returns `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` for a waiter or a chef, and
`503` if the database is unavailable.

200.description: Everybody who works here, active first. Admins only.

post.summary: Adds somebody to the restaurant, with a password they must replace.
post.description:
The response carries the new row and never the password or its hash. What
the admin hands over is what they typed into their own form, which the
browser still has; sending it back would be putting a plain password in a
response body for no gain.

# Errors

Returns `400` naming each field that was not accepted, including
`fields.email=already_taken`, `401` if nobody is signed in, `403` for a
waiter or a chef, and `503` if the database is unavailable.

201.description: The new staff member. Admins only.

patch.summary: Changes somebody's display name. Their sessions are left alone.
patch.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 staff_changed` if the stored version is newer,
`409 staff_inactive` if the account is switched off, `404` for an id this
restaurant does not have, `400` naming the field that was not accepted,
`401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The staff member to rename.

200.description: The updated staff member. Admins only.

409.description: `staff_inactive`, or `staff_changed` if somebody changed them after the form loaded.

post.summary: Switches an account off, and signs their devices out at once.
post.description:
Never refused because of the service. Open visits, unserved rounds, and open
bills keep pointing at the row and this succeeds regardless.

# Errors

Returns `409 cannot_act_on_self`, `409 staff_inactive`, and `409 last_admin`
in that order when more than one applies, `404` for an id this restaurant
does not have, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a waiter or a
chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The staff member to switch off.

200.description: The switched off staff member. Admins only.

409.description: `cannot_act_on_self`, `staff_inactive`, or `last_admin`, reported in that order.

post.summary: Writes a new password onto somebody's row, and signs their devices out.
post.description:
Answers `204`, carrying nothing. The admin already has the password: they
typed it, and their own form is what shows it to them once.

# Errors

Returns `400` with `fields.password` naming the rule it broke,
`409 cannot_act_on_self`, `409 staff_inactive`, `404` for an id this
restaurant does not have, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` for a
waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The staff member whose password is being reset.

204.description: Reset, and every session of theirs ended. Admins only.

409.description: `cannot_act_on_self` or `staff_inactive`.

post.summary: Brings a switched off account back, exactly as it was.
post.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 staff_inactive` if the account is already active, `404` for an
id this restaurant does not have, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403`
for a waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The staff member to bring back.

200.description: The staff member, active again. Admins only.

409.description: `staff_inactive`: the account is already active.

put.summary: Changes what somebody is allowed to be, and signs their devices out.
put.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 cannot_act_on_self`, `409 staff_inactive`, `409 last_admin`,
and `409 staff_changed` in that order when more than one applies, `404` for
an id this restaurant does not have, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403`
for a waiter or a chef.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The staff member whose role is changing.

200.description: The updated staff member. Admins only.

409.description: `cannot_act_on_self`, `staff_inactive`, `last_admin`, or `staff_changed`, reported in that order.

post.summary: Seats a party and opens their bill, in one transaction.
post.description:
Both or neither. A visit with no bill would be a table that could take an
order nobody could be charged for, and it would be discovered at the end of
the meal.

# Errors

Returns `409 table_occupied` if somebody else opened that table first, `400`
if the table is archived or not this restaurant's, `401` if nobody is signed
in, and `403` if the caller is not a waiter.

201.description: The visit and its bill. Waiters only.

409.description: That table already has a party at it.

get.description:
# Errors

Returns `404` if there is no such visit in this restaurant, which is also
the answer for another restaurant's visit so the two cannot be told apart,
`401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The visit to read.

200.description: The visit, its rounds, and its bill. Waiters only.

post.summary: Ends the meal: closes the bill, then closes the visit.
post.description:
In that order and in one transaction. `close_visit` refuses while a bill on
the visit is still open, so the order is not a preference; and one
transaction is what stops a bill being numbered and totalled while its table
stays occupied for ever because the second write failed.

A bill with nothing chargeable on it (nothing ordered, or every dish
cancelled) is voided instead of closed, so it uses no bill number. The
answer then carries `status: voided`, zero figures, and no number, and the
screen says there was nothing to charge.

The lock order and the void live in `billing::end_visit`.

# Errors

Returns `409 bill_has_unserved_lines` if a dish has not reached the table,
`409 bill_already_closed` if somebody closed or voided it first, `404` if
there is no such visit or it has no open bill, `401` if nobody is signed in,
and `403` if the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The visit to close.

200.description: The closed bill, with its number and every figure, or the voided empty bill with none. Waiters only.

404.description: No such visit, or it has no bill.

409.description: A dish is still out, or the bill has already closed.

post.summary:
Moves a party, with their tickets, bill, and responsible waiter, to a free
table.
post.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 table_occupied` if the destination has a party at it, `409
visit_not_open` if the party has left, `404` if there is no such visit or
the destination is archived or unknown, `401` if nobody is signed in, and
`403` if the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The visit to move.

200.description: The party's new table. Waiters only.

404.description: No such visit, or no such live table.

409.description: `table_occupied`: that table has a party at it. `visit_not_open`: the party has left.

post.summary: Sends one ticket to the kitchen and puts its dishes on the bill.
post.description:
One transaction, so a ticket whose lines are on no bill cannot exist. That
is what keeps the bill's running subtotal true throughout the meal and
leaves the close with no assignment left to do.

Safe to repeat: the same `clientKey` again answers `200` with the ticket the
first send made, and writes nothing.

# Errors

Returns `400` if the basket is empty, a quantity is not positive, or a note
is longer than 140 characters (as `fields."lines.N.note" = too_long`), `409
dish_not_orderable` if a dish was switched off or taken off the menu before
the ticket went, which refuses the whole ticket, `409 visit_not_open` if the
party has left, `409 client_key_reused` if the key already sent a ticket for
another visit, `404` if there is no such visit, `401` if nobody is signed
in, and `403` if the caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The visit to send the ticket for.

200.description: An earlier send with the same key already made this ticket; nothing new was sent. Waiters only.

201.description: The ticket that was sent. Waiters only.

400.description: An empty basket, a quantity below one, or a note over 140 characters.

409.description: `visit_not_open`: that party has already left. `dish_not_orderable`: a dish went off before the ticket went, and nothing was sent. `client_key_reused`: that key already sent a ticket for another table.

post.summary:
Makes the caller the responsible waiter for a table, so its ready chime
comes to them.
post.description:
# Errors

Returns `409 table_taken_over` if somebody else became responsible after
the screen was drawn, `409 visit_not_open` if the party has left, `404` if
there is no such visit, `401` if nobody is signed in, and `403` if the
caller is not a waiter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The visit to take over.

200.description: The caller is now responsible. Waiters only.

409.description: `table_taken_over`: somebody else took it first. `visit_not_open`: the party has left.

AdminCategoryDto.description: One live category with its dishes.

dishes.description: Its live dishes, in printed order.

version.description: Which edit of the category this is. Send it back with a rename.

id.description: Which section this is, or `null` for the no section group.

name.description: What it is called, or `null` for the no section group.

tables.description: Its live tables, in displayed order.

version.description:
Which edit of the section this is, or `null` for the no section group.
Send it back with a rename.

AdminFloorResponse.description: The whole floor as the admin works on it, live and archived.

archived.description: What has been taken off the floor and can be put back.

AdminMenuResponse.description: The whole menu as the admin works on it, live and archived.

archived.description: What has been taken off the menu and can be put back.

categories.description:
Every live category in printed order, each with every live dish in it,
available or not. Unlike the ordering menu, an empty category is kept:
it is exactly the one an admin is about to fill.

currencyDecimals.description:
How many decimal places that currency uses, which is also how many a
price may carry.

AdminTableDto.description: One live table on the admin's floor.

occupied.description:
Whether a party is at it right now. A table with a party at it cannot
be removed.

seats.description: How many it seats, when recorded.

version.description: Which edit of the table this is. Send it back with an edit.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the menu.

ArchivedDishDto.description: One archived dish, with what the restore dialog needs.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the menu.

categoryId.description: The category it was in when it was removed.

categoryLive.description:
Whether that category is still live. The restore dialog offers it as
the default only when it is.

categoryName.description:
What that category is called, carried here because it may be archived
too and so appear nowhere else on the screen.

diet.description: Whether it is veg, non veg, or egg.

sections.description: Archived sections, most recently removed first.

tables.description: Every archived table, in the order they stood before removal.

categories.description: Archived categories, most recently removed first.

dishes.description: Archived dishes, most recently removed first.

ArchivedSectionDto.description:
One archived section, with the archived tables a restore can bring back
with it.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the floor.

tables.description: The archived tables whose section is this one, in their old order.

ArchivedSectionTableDto.description: One table a section restore can bring back.

seats.description: How many it seated, when recorded.

ArchivedTableDto.description: One archived table, with what the restore dialog needs.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the floor.

seats.description: How many it seated, when recorded.

sectionId.description: The section it was in when it was removed, if any.

sectionLive.description:
Whether that section is still live. The restore dialog offers it as the
default only when it is.

sectionName.description:
What that section is called, carried here because it may be archived
too and so appear nowhere else on the screen.

BillDto.description:
A bill, open or closed, with every figure it currently carries.

The currency travels with it rather than being read from the restaurant,
because a closed bill keeps the currency it was charged in even after the
restaurant changes. A screen formatting a bill must use these two and not
the restaurant's current pair.

closedAt.description: When it closed, if it has.

currencyDecimals.description: How many decimal places that currency uses.

number.description: Its number within the restaurant, allocated at close. `null` while open.

serviceChargeAmount.description: What that rate came to. Zero rather than null when there is none.

serviceChargePercent.description:
The service charge rate applied, or `null` when the restaurant charges
none.

status.description: Whether it is still collecting dishes.

subtotal.description: The sum of its dishes that were not cancelled.

taxTotal.description: The sum of the tax lines.

taxes.description: The tax breakdown, empty until it closes.

total.description: Subtotal plus service charge plus taxes, with no residue.

BillTaxDto.description: One tax line copied onto a bill when it closed.

amount.description: What that came to, already rounded to the bill's currency.

name.description: What the tax was called at the time.

ratePercent.description: What rate was charged, as an exact decimal string.

CategoryDto.description: One category, as a write on it answers.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the menu, or `null` while it is on it.

version.description: Which edit of the category this is.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: What changing your own password asks for.

currentPassword.description: The password they are signing in with now.

newPassword.description: What they want it to be.

ChangeRoleRequest.description: What changing somebody's role asks for.

role.description: What they should be allowed to be.

version.description: The version the form loaded. An older one is refused as stale.

CreateCategoryRequest.description: What adding a category asks for.

name.description:
What it is called. At most 60 characters, unique among live categories
ignoring letter case.

CreateDishRequest.description:
What adding a dish asks for.

No availability: a new dish is available, and only the switch changes that.
No position: it goes to the end of its category.

categoryId.description: Which live category it goes in.

description.description: What it is, for the waiter to read out. At most 300 characters.

diet.description: Whether it is veg, non veg, or egg. Required.

name.description:
What it is called. At most 80 characters, unique among live dishes
ignoring letter case.

price.description:
What it costs, as a decimal string such as `"320.50"`. Never a JSON
number. Zero or more, below ten billion, and no more decimal places than
the restaurant's currency uses.

CreateSectionRequest.description: What adding a section asks for.

name.description:
What it is called. At most 40 characters, unique among live sections
ignoring letter case.

CreateStaffRequest.description: What creating a member of staff asks for.

displayName.description: What to call them on screen. At most 80 characters once trimmed.

email.description: The address they will sign in with. Unique across the whole platform.

password.description:
The password the admin is about to hand them. They must replace it
before they can do anything else.

role.description: What they are allowed to be.

CreateTableRangeRequest.description: What adding a numbered range of tables asks for.

prefix.description:
Written before each number. Leading spaces are removed and trailing
ones kept, so `"Bar "` gives `Bar 1`. Absent or blank means bare
numbers.

seats.description: How many each table seats, a whole number from 1 to 50, or `null`.

sectionId.description: Which live section every table goes in, or `null` for none.

to.description:
The last number, 1 to 999, not below `from`, and at most 50 tables in
all.

CreateTableRequest.description: What adding one table asks for.

label.description:
What the staff call it. At most 12 characters, unique among the
restaurant's live tables ignoring letter case.

seats.description: How many it seats, a whole number from 1 to 50, or `null`.

sectionId.description: Which live section it goes in, or `null` for none.

DietDto.description:
Whether a dish is veg, non veg, or egg, on the wire.

The same three words the `dish_diet` enum stores, kept that way by the test
at the foot of this file.

DishDto.description:
One dish, with everything an admin's edit form needs.

What every menu write answers with, and what the admin menu lists. The
`version` is the one the form sends back, which is how an edit made from a
stale form is told apart from a current one.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the menu, or `null` while it is on it.

available.description: Whether the kitchen can make it right now.

description.description: What it is, for the waiter to read out. `null` when there is none.

diet.description: Whether it is veg, non veg, or egg.

price.description: What it costs, as an exact decimal string. Never a JSON number.

version.description: Which edit of the dish this is. Send it back with an edit.

EditDishRequest.description:
What editing a dish asks for: everything the dish should be, and which
version of it the form loaded.

No availability. Only the switch writes that, so an edit form opened before
the kitchen switched a dish off cannot switch it back on; the switch bumps
the version, and the form's save is refused as stale.

categoryId.description:
Which live category it should sit under. A different one moves it to
the end of that category.

description.description: What it is, or `null` for no description.

diet.description: Whether it is veg, non veg, or egg.

price.description:
What it should cost, as a decimal string. Lines already sent keep the
price they copied.

version.description: The version the edit form loaded.
The version the edit form loaded. An older one is refused as stale.

EditTableRequest.description:
What editing a table asks for: everything the table should be, and which
version of it the form loaded.

label.description: What the staff should call it.

sectionId.description:
Which live section it should be in, or `null` for none. A different
group moves it to the end of that group.

version.description: The version the edit form loaded.

ErrorBody.description: The body every failed request returns.

error.description:
A stable machine readable code, safe to branch on in the client.

A refused conflict names which conflict it was, such as
`table_occupied` or `bill_has_unserved_lines`, rather than the blanket
word `conflict`. The closed list is
[`ConflictKind`](crate::domain::error::ConflictKind).

fields.description:
What is wrong with each named field, when the problem is a form rather
than the request as a whole.

Absent from every response that has no field level problem, which is
most of them, so nothing that was already reading this body changes.
Each value is one of a closed set of codes: `already_taken`,
`too_short`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`, `unknown_country`,
`not_in_catalogue`, `incorrect`, `required`, `not_a_number`,
`negative`, `too_large`, `too_many_decimals`, `too_small`,
`before_start`, `too_many`.

labels.description:
The labels that clashed, present only on `409 labels_taken` and absent
from every other response.

Spelled and ordered as the request would have created them. Empty when
a label was taken between the check and the write and nothing clashes
any more, which a screen reads as "try again".

message.description:
A human readable sentence. Never contains internal detail.

English, and for a log. The web app renders a translation of
[`Self::error`] instead, because the API is a data API and knows nothing
about what language anybody reads.
message.example: The requested resource does not exist.

FloorResponse.description: Every table in the restaurant, grouped by section.

sections.description: The sections, in displayed order, each with its tables.

id.description:
Which section this is, or `null` for the group holding tables that
belong to no live section.

name.description:
What it is called, or `null` for that same group. A screen shows those
tables under a heading of its own choosing, in its own language.

FloorTableDto.description: One table, and whoever is sitting at it.

label.description: What the staff call it, such as `12` or `Bar 3`.

oneOf.description: Who is at it, or `null` when it is free.

seats.description: How many it seats, when the restaurant recorded it.

HealthResponse.description:
What the health endpoint returns.

A presentation DTO rather than the application's `HealthReport`, so that the
wire format can change without touching a use case, and so that no inner
layer has to know the `utoipa` schema traits exist.

listener.description: Whether this instance's Postgres listen connection is up.

serving.description: True only when every dependency is up.

IdentityBundle.description:
Everything the browser needs to know who it is talking for.

Returned identically by register, sign in, `GET /api/me`, `PATCH /api/me`,
and `PATCH /api/restaurant`, so the browser has one type and one cache
entry. Five endpoints returning five nearly identical shapes is how a client
ends up with five slightly different ideas of who is signed in.

KitchenLineDto.description:
One dish on a kitchen ticket.

Deliberately narrower than [`OrderLineDto`]. A kitchen screen has no
business showing a price, and a chef tapping a dish done should not be one
misread column away from the bill.

id.description: Which line this is. What the mark ready call names.

note.description: What the guest asked for, such as no onions. Reaches the pass unchanged.

status.description: Where this one dish has got to.

voidReason.description:
The words whoever cancelled it gave. Carried only for `other`, the one
code that says nothing on its own and the one code that requires them;
for the other three the code is the reason and the words are a note to a
manager rather than to the kitchen.

oneOf.description:
Why it was cancelled, for a dish in the Cancelled strip. The screen says
it in its own language from this code; the free text behind it is the
waiter's own words and does not belong on a wall screen. `null` for a
dish that was not cancelled.

KitchenResponse.description: Everything the kitchen still has work on.

lateAfterSeconds.description: After how many seconds it draws one red.

serverTime.description:
What the server's clock reads, at the moment this answer was built.

The screen subtracts this from its own clock and corrects every age it
draws by the difference. A kitchen tablet whose clock is twenty minutes
fast would otherwise show every ticket as twenty minutes late, and the
one number a chef acts on would be the one number nobody could trust.

truncatedCount.description:
How many more tickets there were than this answer carries. `0` means
nothing was left out, which is every ordinary evening. Above zero, the
screen says work is hidden rather than hiding it silently.

warningAfterSeconds.description:
After how many seconds of waiting the screen draws a ticket amber. This
restaurant's own setting, not a number the screen decides.

KitchenTicketDto.description: One ticket on the kitchen screen.

lines.description: Every dish on it, oldest first.

readyAt.description:
When the last dish came off the pass, for a ticket that is ready. A
plated ticket's age is measured from here instead, because what matters
about it is how long it has been under the lamp. `null` while it is still
cooking.

sentAt.description: When it reached the kitchen. A cooking ticket's age is measured from here.

sequenceNo.description: Its number within the visit, so a chef can say "table 4, second round".

status.description: Where the whole ticket has got to.

LineStatusDto.description: Where one dish has got to, on the wire.

roundStatus.description:
What the whole ticket became, recomputed from all of its dishes. The
kitchen screen uses this to drop a ticket that has just gone ready.

available.description:
Whether the kitchen can make it right now. `false` greys it on the
ordering screen and stops it being added to a basket.

description.description: What it is, for the waiter to read out.

diet.description: Whether it is veg, non veg, or egg, drawn as the square mark.

price.description: What it costs, as an exact decimal string. Never a JSON number.

MenuResponse.description: The whole menu, grouped the way it is printed.

categories.description:
The live categories, in printed order. A category with no live dish is
left out, because an empty heading on a phone is a row of wasted space.

currencyCode.description:
What this restaurant charges in. Carried here rather than left to the
screen to look up, so a price and the currency it is in arrive together.

currencyDecimals.description: How many decimal places that currency uses.

MoveVisitRequest.description: What moving a party asks for.

tableId.description: The free, live table they are moving to.
The table they are at now.

OccupancyDto.description: What a waiter needs to know about an occupied table without opening it.

guestCount.description: How many of them, when the waiter recorded it.

openedBy.description: What to call the waiter who seated them.

readyDishCount.description: How many dishes on this visit are waiting to be carried out.

responsibleStaffId.description: The waiter who hears the ready chime for this table.

visitId.description: The one open visit on this table.

OpenOrderDto.description: One open table on the Orders list.

responsibleStaffId.description: The waiter who hears the ready chime for this table.

rounds.description: Every ticket on the visit, oldest first, with its dishes.

tableLabel.description: What the staff call that table.

OpenOrdersResponse.description: Every open table in the restaurant, with every ticket on it.

serverTime.description:
What the server's clock reads, at the moment this answer was built. The
screen corrects every age it draws by the difference from its own clock.

visits.description:
The open visits, in the order they were opened. The screen sorts them
by what is ready.

OpenVisitRequest.description: What seating a party asks for.

guestCount.description: How many of them, if the waiter counted.

tableId.description: Which table they are sitting at.

OpenVisitResponse.description: The visit and the bill that were created together.

billId.description: The bill their dishes will go on.

visitId.description: The party's stay at the table.

OrderLineDto.description:
One dish on one ticket, as every screen reads it.

The name and the price are the ones copied onto the line when the round was
sent, not today's menu. That is what lets a bill from last Tuesday stay
true after a reprice.

dishId.description: Which menu item it came from.

dishName.description: What the dish was called when it was ordered.

lineTotal.description: Quantity times unit price, as an exact decimal string.

note.description: What the guest asked for, such as no onions.

readyAt.description:
When it came off the pass. How long ready food has waited is measured
from here.

status.description: Where this one dish has got to.

unitPrice.description: What one of them cost, as an exact decimal string.

voidReason.description: The waiter's own words about why, when they gave any.

oneOf.description: Why it was cancelled, on a cancelled dish.

lines.description: Every dish on it, oldest first.

readyAt.description: When the last dish came off the pass.

sequenceNo.description: Its number within the visit, starting at one.

servedAt.description: When the last dish reached the table.

status.description: Where the whole ticket has got to, recomputed from its dishes.

RegisterRequest.description:
What registration asks for.

Five fields, and that is the product decision showing through: trying this
costs a minute, not an afternoon of settings. Everything else about the
restaurant is derived from the country or changed later.

countryCode.description:
Where the restaurant is, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Accepted in any
case.

displayName.description: What to call the owner on screen.

email.description: The address they will sign in with.

RenameCategoryRequest.description: What renaming a category asks for.

version.description: The version the rename form loaded. An older one is refused as stale.

RenameSectionRequest.description: What renaming a section asks for.

version.description: The version the rename form loaded. An older one is refused as stale.

ReorderRequest.description:
What a reorder asks for: the complete list, in its new order.

The whole list rather than a move, so the server never has to guess what
"after that one" meant when the list changed underneath the drag. A list
that is not exactly the live set is refused with `409 menu_changed`.

ids.description: Every live id in the list, each exactly once, in the new order.

ResetPasswordRequest.description:
What resetting somebody's password asks for.

No version. An admin resetting a password has decided this person needs a
new one, and whether somebody renamed them meanwhile does not change that.

password.description: The password the admin is about to hand them.

RestaurantDto.description:
The restaurant the signed in person works at, as every screen reads it.

Carries the five settings spec 0005's formatting layer needs and nothing
about money beyond the currency: figures on a bill come from the bill.

address.description: Where it is, for printing on a bill. `null` when nobody has set one.

countryCode.description: Where it is, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

currencyDecimals.description: How many decimal places that currency uses.

defaultLanguage.description:
What the kitchen screen reads, and the fallback for anybody with no
personal setting.

formattingLocale.description:
How money, numbers, dates, and times are written here. Deliberately not
derived from the language.

kitchenLateAfterSeconds.description: After how many seconds it draws one red. Always the larger of the two.

kitchenWarningAfterSeconds.description: After how many seconds the kitchen pass draws a waiting ticket amber.

timezone.description:
Its own IANA timezone. Every timestamp on a screen is converted with it,
never with the device's.

version.description:
Which version of this row the screen is holding. An edit has to name it,
and one naming an older version is refused rather than merged over
somebody else's change. Carried on every identity bundle, including the
one a successful save returns, so a screen that just saved holds the new
version without a second read.

RestoreDishRequest.description: What restoring a dish asks for.

categoryId.description:
Which live category to put it in. The dialog offers the dish's old one
when that is still live.

RestoreSectionRequest.description: What restoring a section asks for.

tableIds.description:
The archived tables of this section to bring back with it. May be
empty. Each must be an archived table whose section is this one.

RestoreTableRequest.description: What restoring a table asks for.

sectionId.description:
Which live section to put it in, or `null` for none. The dialog offers
the table's old section when that is still live.

RestoredSectionDto.description: A restored section and the tables that came back with it.

section.description: The section, live again at the end of the list.

tables.description: The tables restored into it, in their order.

RoleDto.description:
What a member of staff is allowed to be, on the wire.

A separate enum from [`StaffRole`] because that one lives in the domain and
may not learn that `utoipa` exists. The strings are identical, and the two
tests below are what keep them that way.

RoundStatusDto.description: Where a whole ticket has got to, on the wire.

SectionDto.description: One section, as a write on it answers.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the floor, or `null` while it is on it.

version.description: Which edit of the section this is.

SectionOrderRequest.description: What reordering the sections asks for: the complete list, in its new order.

ids.description: Every live section id, each exactly once, in the new order.

note.description:
What the guest asked for, such as no onions. At most 140 characters
after trimming; blank is the same as none.

SendRoundRequest.description:
What sending a ticket asks for.

No price anywhere in it, and that is the point. The price and the name are
read from the dish inside `send_round` and copied onto the line, so a client
cannot name its own price however it is built.

clientKey.description:
A key the phone made for this basket, the same on every retry until one
send succeeds. A key the server already holds for this visit sends
nothing new and answers with the first ticket.

lines.description: The basket, one entry per dish. At least one.

SetAvailabilityRequest.description: What the availability switch asks for.

available.description:
What the dish should be: `true` for orderable, `false` for off. An
absolute value, never a toggle, so two quick taps cannot cancel out.

email.description: The address the account was registered with. Matched case insensitively.

StaffDto.description: Who the signed in person is.

displayName.description: What to call them on screen.

email.description:
The address they sign in with, exactly as they typed it when they
registered. Handed back unflattened so the account screen shows them
their own capitalisation.

id.description:
Which staff member this is.

A bare uuid rather than the domain's `StaffId`, because a newtype in
`domain/` may not learn that `utoipa` exists. The wire has always been
where identifiers lose their types.

language.description:
Their own interface language, or `null` for "whatever the restaurant
uses", which is what a new account has.

mustChangePassword.description:
Whether an admin wrote the password they are signed in with, so they owe
their own before they can do anything else.

On the bundle rather than on an endpoint of its own, because every
screen has to know it and the browser already holds exactly one copy of
this bundle. A second endpoint would be a second answer, and the two
would disagree the moment one of them was refetched.

role.description: What they are allowed to be.

StaffListResponse.description: Everybody who works here, in one response.

staff.description:
Active people first, then by display name ignoring letter case, then by
id. Deactivated people are included, in the section below.

StaffMemberDto.description:
One member of staff, as the admin's staff screen reads them.

A separate shape from [`StaffDto`], which is about the person signed in.
This one is about somebody else, so it carries what an admin needs to decide
what to do next (are they switched on, have they ever managed to sign in, do
they still owe a password) and what an edit needs to be safe (the version).
It carries no language, because that is theirs to choose and not an admin's
to see.

active.description: Whether the account is switched on.

displayName.description: What to call them on screen.

email.description: The address they sign in with, exactly as it was typed.

lastSignInAt.description:
When they last signed in. `null` means never, which is how an admin
spots a typed address that nobody could ever have used.

mustChangePassword.description: Whether they still owe their own password.

role.description: What they are allowed to be.

version.description: Which edit of the row this is. Send it back with an edit.

StreamEvent.description:
What one message on the stream looks like.

A kind and an id, never row content. The client uses it to refetch or to
patch its query cache, which keeps row level security the single authority
on who may see what: a client that should not see a row simply gets nothing
back when it asks for it.

entity.description: What kind of thing changed, for example `probe`.

TableDto.description: One table, as a write on it answers.

archivedAt.description: When it was taken off the floor, or `null` while it is on it.

seats.description: How many it seats, when recorded.

sectionId.description: Which section it is in, or `null`.

version.description: Which edit of the table this is.

TableOrderRequest.description: What reordering one group of tables asks for.

ids.description: Every live table of that group, each exactly once, in the new order.

sectionId.description: Which group: a live section, or `null` for the no section group.

TakeOverRequest.description: What taking over a table asks for.

expectedStaffId.description:
The waiter the screen showed as responsible. If somebody else has taken
the table since, the request is refused rather than taking it from them.

TakeOverResponse.description: Who is responsible for a table now.

UpdateMeRequest.description:
What somebody may change about their own account.

Both fields are optional and absent means "leave it alone". `language` is
deliberately `Option<Option<String>>`: absent leaves it, and an explicit
`null` clears it, which is a real choice somebody makes rather than an
absence. Collapsing the two would make "follow the restaurant" unsayable.

displayName.description: What to call them on screen.

language.description:
Their own interface language, or `null` to follow the restaurant.

Clippy is overruled here, and the reason is the whole point of the
field. The three states are genuinely different and all three have to be
sayable: absent means "do not touch my language", `null` means "follow
the restaurant", and a code means that code. A custom enum would say the
same thing with a hand written `Deserialize` and a hand written
`ToSchema`, and the wire shape would be identical.

UpdateRestaurantRequest.description:
What an admin may change about the restaurant.

No money setting appears here at all. The currency and its decimals were
fixed by the country at registration and changing them under bills that have
already closed would rewrite history.

address.description: Where it is, for printing on a bill. An empty string clears it.

formattingLocale.description: How it writes money, numbers, and dates.

kitchenLateAfterSeconds.description:
After how many seconds it draws one red. The same bounds, and above the
warning threshold.

kitchenWarningAfterSeconds.description:
After how many seconds the kitchen pass draws a waiting ticket amber.
Between 60 and 14400, and below the late threshold once laid over what is
stored.

version.description:
Which version of the restaurant this edit was made against. Required, and
an edit naming one that is no longer current is refused rather than
merged over somebody else's change. Every identity bundle carries it,
including the one a successful save returns.

VisitResponse.description: One table's whole meal, as the waiter's screen reads it.

oneOf.description:
The bill, with its running subtotal while open and every figure once
closed. `null` only for a visit that somehow has none.

guestCount.description: How many of them, when the waiter recorded it.

openedBy.description: What to call the waiter who seated them.

responsibleStaffId.description: The waiter who hears the ready chime for this table.

rounds.description: Every ticket on the visit, oldest first, with its dishes.

serverTime.description:
What the server's clock reads, at the moment this answer was built. The
screen corrects every age it draws by the difference from its own clock.

status.description: Whether they are still there: `open` or `closed`.

tableLabel.description: What the staff call that table.

VoidLineRequest.description: What cancelling a dish asks for.

reason.description:
The waiter's own words. Required for `other`, optional otherwise, at
most 200 characters.

billSubtotal.description:
The bill's running subtotal after the dish came off it, as an exact
decimal string. `null` for a dish on no bill.

roundStatus.description: What the whole ticket became, recomputed from all of its dishes.

VoidReasonDto.description: Why a dish was cancelled, on the wire.
